title: Memento: An Adaptive, Compiler-Assisted Register File Cache for GPUs
problem: Modern GPUs require enormous register files to store context for thousands of active threads, which consume significant energy and have multiple banks causing port conflicts and throughput limitations.
motivation: Improving register file efficiency can significantly reduce GPU energy consumption and performance penalties from costly register bank accesses.
method: Memento builds a cache for the register file (where GPUs store active thread data) using hardware that's already in the GPU. Before the program runs, a compiler uses profiling (running test cases to observe patterns) to estimate value reuse distances—how many instructions apart each value is used again. At runtime, the GPU uses these predictions to decide when to fetch values from the cache instead of the main register file, and continuously adapts this strategy based on what the program actually does.
key_novelty: Memento uses compiler-predicted value reuse distances to guide adaptive runtime decisions about which register values to cache, building the cache from existing hardware instead of adding new components.
contributions: Energy-efficient RF caching mechanism that leverages existing GPU components
Compiler-assisted reuse distance profiling to guide cache scheduling decisions
Dynamic adaptive issue scheduling policy that responds to runtime program characteristics
Achieves 28.3% RF energy reduction and 6.1% performance improvement with only 0.78% storage overhead

metrics.energy_or_tops_w: 28.3% reduction in RF dynamic energy, 46.4% reduction in RF bank reads

baselines: baseline GPU register file without RF cache
primary_theme: Energy-efficient GPU register file caching with compiler-assisted adaptive scheduling
